researchAreas.title: AI & Technology
researchAreas.summary: Foundational models, infrastructure, capabilities, and the dynamics of AI advancement.
researchAreas.overview: AI & Technology examines technical capability, infrastructure, model behaviour, and the institutional conditions that shape how AI systems become usable or risky.
researchAreas.why_it_matters: Technical change only becomes consequential when it meets incentives, workflows, policy, and human interpretation. This area keeps capability signals connected to decisions and consequences.
researchAreas.methodological_note: Analysis separates observed technical signals from institutional inference and avoids unsupported claims about capability, adoption, or impact.

researchAreas.title: Institutions & Governance
researchAreas.summary: Power structures, incentives, policies, and governance transformation.
researchAreas.overview: Institutions & Governance studies how rules, incentives, standards, and operating models shape public-interest decisions.
researchAreas.why_it_matters: Governance failures often occur between policy intent and practical use. This area focuses on the translation layer where institutions turn analysis into action.
researchAreas.methodological_note: Outputs distinguish governance structure, decision context, and implementation constraints rather than treating policy as a finished endpoint.

researchAreas.title: Society & Behavior
researchAreas.summary: Attention, culture, human behavior, and the shifting social operating system.
researchAreas.overview: Society & Behavior examines attention, trust, interaction patterns, cultural incentives, and how people interpret emerging systems.
researchAreas.why_it_matters: Signals become consequential through human behaviour. This area keeps interpretation, social context, and public-facing consequences visible.
researchAreas.methodological_note: Research avoids clinical, therapeutic, or direct-support positioning and focuses on prevention-oriented public-interest analysis.

researchAreas.title: Economy & Work
researchAreas.summary: Labor markets, productivity, organizational change, and value creation.
researchAreas.overview: Economy & Work studies how innovation, labour, organisational systems, and funding environments change what institutions can do.
researchAreas.why_it_matters: Economic and organisational consequences determine whether technological change creates usable public value or new systemic pressure.
researchAreas.methodological_note: Analysis treats economic change as a signal environment and avoids unsupported forecasts, market claims, or fabricated traction.

researchAreas.title: Risk & Futures
researchAreas.summary: Emerging risks, systemic vulnerabilities, and plausible future scenarios.
researchAreas.overview: Risk & Futures maps weak signals, institutional blind spots, plausible scenarios, and the decision windows around emerging risks.
researchAreas.why_it_matters: The value of foresight is not prediction. It is clearer interpretation of signals before consequences become locked in.
researchAreas.methodological_note: Scenario work is labelled as inference, not forecast, and is tied back to evidence, boundaries, and decision relevance.

programmes.title: Policy Usability & Decision Systems
programmes.summary: Research on how policy outputs become usable at the point of decision.
programmes.overview: This programme studies the missing translation layer between policy, analysis, and institutional decisions.
research_questions: How do decision-makers interpret policy outputs under time, uncertainty, and operational pressure?
What makes a policy signal usable at the point where choices are made?
Which structures help institutions convert analysis into decision-ready guidance?
programmes.methodology: Decision-context mapping, policy-output review, institutional boundary analysis, and translation-layer modelling.

programmes.title: Youth Safety & Emerging Risks
programmes.summary: Prevention-focused intelligence on emerging risks affecting children and young people.
programmes.overview: This programme examines emerging risk signals in youth-facing digital environments without positioning Singulary as a crisis, therapeutic, legal, or direct survivor-support service.
research_questions: Which weak signals suggest emerging youth-facing risk patterns?
How can institutions identify prevention windows before risk patterns normalise?
What boundaries are needed for responsible public-interest analysis?
programmes.methodology: Prevention-focused signal collection, source review, scenario mapping, methodological boundary checks, and responsible interpretation.

programmes.title: Innovation Intelligence & Signal Detection
programmes.summary: Monitoring weak signals and institutional shifts in innovation ecosystems.
programmes.overview: This programme monitors weak signals across technology, institutions, society, work, and plausible futures.
research_questions: Which signals indicate shifts in innovation capability or institutional readiness?
How can noisy information be structured into decision-relevant intelligence?
Where do technical, social, and economic signals converge?
programmes.methodology: Signal tagging, source registry maintenance, cross-domain interpretation, and consequence mapping.

programmes.title: European Innovation Ecosystems
programmes.summary: Research on European innovation infrastructure, funding systems, and policy translation.
programmes.overview: This programme studies European innovation infrastructure and the institutional conditions that shape funding, adoption, and public-interest outcomes.
research_questions: How do European innovation systems translate funding and policy into usable capacity?
Where do governance, markets, and institutional incentives create friction?
What signals indicate stronger public-interest innovation infrastructure?
programmes.methodology: Institutional mapping, policy-system review, ecosystem signal analysis, and decision-context interpretation.
